items.title: Tommy Newsom and Ross Tompkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995
items.q: Or Sweets Edison. Did you happen to hear him play?

ctx.x: It keeps going around, you know.

If acoustic stays out long enough, it might be the new thing in a while, you know, if people get enough of digitally produced sounds, they might—if they hear guys, like hear Snooky Young play. Or Sweets Edison. Did you happen to hear him play?
We talked to him. We didn’t get to hear him.

items.title: Tommy Newsom and Ross Tompkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995
items.q: The interviewee only responds to the interviewer's mention of the '38 band with Sweets... and Buck', without adding personal anecdotes or confirming a direct personal relationship.

ctx.x: Yeah. It was that nice thing.

Because Zoot and I used to argue. I was very fond of that band, of that period when Snooky was playing lead, you know, Sonny Payne, Eddie Jones. And Zoot and I used to argue whether the ‘38 band with Sweets and Buck and all those guys, which one was better. And they were both great. I think probably the one from the 60s might be a little rehearsed a little more or something.
Yeah, but the earlier band was like an original.
